Command: Do not eat the fat of ox, sheep, or goat
Summary: The fat of ox, sheep, or goat — the fat belonging to the LORD's offerings — may not be eaten, in any dwelling.
Commandment: Do not eat the fat of ox, of sheep, or of goat.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The fat was the LORD's portion on the altar; keeping it from the table taught Israel that the best belonged to God. Hebrews teaches the sacrificial system pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14).
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
